Messi was named Barcelona's captain in 2018. While playing for the club, he won a [club-record](/wiki/List_of_FC_Barcelona_records_and_statistics#Other_individual_records_for_the_club "List of FC Barcelona records and statistics") 34 trophies, including ten La Liga titles and four [UEFA Champions Leagues](/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League"). Financial difficulties at Barcelona led Messi to depart in August 2021 and sign with [Paris Saint-Germain](/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain "Paris Saint-Germain"), where he won the [Ligue 1](/wiki/Ligue_1 "Ligue 1") title during both of his seasons there. He joined the Major League Soccer club Inter Miami in July 2023, and led them to their first [MLS Cup](/wiki/MLS_Cup "MLS Cup") victory in [2025](/wiki/MLS_Cup_2025 "MLS Cup 2025"), while also winning back-to-back [league MVP awards](/wiki/Landon_Donovan_MVP_Award "Landon Donovan MVP Award") in [2024](/wiki/2024_Major_League_Soccer_season "2024 Major League Soccer season") and [2025](/wiki/2025_Major_League_Soccer_season "2025 Major League Soccer season").

An Argentine international, Messi is the national team's [all-time leading goalscorer](/wiki/Argentina_national_football_team#Top_goalscorers "Argentina national football team") and [most-capped player](/wiki/Argentina_national_football_team#Most_appearances "Argentina national football team"). Several years after his senior debut in 2005, he won the [gold medal](/wiki/Olympic_medal "Olympic medal") at the [2008 Summer Olympics](/wiki/Football_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men%27s_tournament "Football at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament"). [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/Californian_Lone_Star_Flag_%281836%29.svg/250px-Californian_Lone_Star_Flag_%281836%29.svg.png)](/wiki/File:Californian_Lone_Star_Flag_(1836).svg)

The lone star of the 1836 California Lone Star Flag used by [Juan Bautista Alvarado](/wiki/Juan_Bautista_Alvarado "Juan Bautista Alvarado"), which inspired the red star in the flag of the Bear Flag Revolt.

In 1836, a coup led by [Juan Alvarado](/wiki/Juan_Bautista_Alvarado "Juan Bautista Alvarado") declared Alta California's independence from Mexico. Alvarado declared himself governor of the territory and raised a banner with the inscription: "FEDERATION OR DEATH."[[20]](#cite_note-20) Alvarado soon recruited U.S. frontiersmen led by [Isaac Graham](/wiki/Isaac_Graham "Isaac Graham"), to support him. The rebels easily captured the capital [Monterey](/wiki/Monterey "Monterey"), but were unable to convince southern leaders such as [Juan Bandini](/wiki/Juan_Bandini "Juan Bandini") and [Carlos Antonio Carrillo](/wiki/Carlos_Antonio_Carrillo "Carlos Antonio Carrillo") to join the rebellion. Faced with a civil war, Alvarado and the other *Californios* negotiated a compromise with the central government wherein California's leaders accepted its status as a "department" under the "[Siete Leyes](/wiki/Siete_Leyes "Siete Leyes")" Mexican constitution of 1836, in return for more local control. Alvarado was appointed governor the next year.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f9/Alvarado%27s_Banner_of_November_6%2C_1836.png/250px-Alvarado%27s_Banner_of_November_6%2C_1836.png)](/wiki/File:Alvarado%27s_Banner_of_November_6,_1836.png)

The banner carried by Alvarado after he declared himself governor[[21]](#cite_note-21)

Golden eagle flying in dihedral with food

Golden eagles are sometimes considered the best fliers among eagles and perhaps among all raptorial birds.[[17]](#cite_note-Leslie-17) They are equipped with broad, long wings with somewhat finger-like indentations on the tips of the wing.[[15]](#cite_note-Ferguson-Lees-15) Golden eagles are unique among their genus in that they often fly in a slight [dihedral](/wiki/Dihedral_(aeronautics) "Dihedral (aeronautics)"), which means the wings are often held in a slight, upturned V-shape.[[15]](#cite_note-Ferguson-Lees-15) When they need to flap, golden eagles appear at their most laboured, but this is less common than soaring or gliding.[[4]](#cite_note-Watson-4) Flapping flight usually consists of 6–8 deep wing-beats, interspersed with 2–3 second glides.[[4]](#cite_note-Watson-4) While soaring, the wings and tail are held in one plane with the primary tips often spread.[[50]](#cite_note-SanDiego-50)

A typical, unhurried soaring speed in golden eagles is around 45–52 kilometres per hour (28–32 mph).[[51]](#cite_note-ADW-51) When hunting or displaying, the golden eagle can glide very fast, reaching speeds of up to 190 kilometres per hour (120 mph).[[4]](#cite_note-Watson-4)[[50]](#cite_note-SanDiego-50) When stooping (diving) in the direction of prey or during territorial displays, the eagle holds its legs up against its tail, and holds its wings tight and partially closed against its body. fanoutqa_015108.x:
COVID-19 pandemic in India :: Timeline :: 2020 :: chunk_0001
On 12 January 2020, the [WHO](/wiki/World_Health_Organization "World Health Organization") confirmed that a [novel coronavirus](/wiki/Novel_coronavirus "Novel coronavirus") was the cause of a respiratory illness in a cluster of people in [Wuhan, Hubei, China](/wiki/Wuhan "Wuhan"), which was reported to the WHO on 31 December 2019.[[30]](#cite_note-Reynolds4March2020-30)

On 30 January 2020, India reported its first case of COVID-19 in [Thrissur](/wiki/Thrissur "Thrissur"), Kerala,[[18]](#cite_note-Andrews-2020-18) which rose to three cases by 3 February 2020; all were students returning from Wuhan.[[31]](#cite_note-Raza2020-31) Apart from these, no significant rise in transmissions was observed in February. On 4 March 22 new cases were reported, including 14 infected members of an Italian tourist group.[[32]](#cite_note-32) Transmissions increased over the month after several people with travel history to affected countries, and their contacts, tested positive.[[33]](#cite_note-33) On 12 March, a 76-year-old man, with a travel history to Saudi Arabia, became the first COVID-19 fatality of India.[[34]](#cite_note-death1-34)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fd/2018_SOTU_27628831.jpg/250px-2018_SOTU_27628831.jpg)](/wiki/File:2018_SOTU_27628831.jpg)

President [Donald Trump](/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") delivers his [2018 State of the Union Address](/wiki/2018_State_of_the_Union_Address "2018 State of the Union Address") before [Congress](/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress").

For most of American history, candidates for president have sought election on the basis of a promised legislative agenda. [Article II, Section 3, Clause 2](/wiki/Article_Two_of_the_United_States_Constitution#Section_3:_Presidential_responsibilities "Article Two of the United States Constitution") requires the president to recommend such measures to Congress which the president deems "necessary and expedient". This is done through the constitutionally based [State of the Union](/wiki/State_of_the_Union "State of the Union") address, which usually outlines the president's legislative proposals for the coming year, and through other formal and informal communications with Congress.

The president can be involved in crafting legislation by suggesting, requesting, or even insisting that Congress enact laws that the president believes are needed. Additionally, the president can attempt to shape legislation during the legislative process by exerting influence on individual members of Congress.[[68]](#cite_note-74) Presidents possess this power because the Constitution is silent about who can write legislation, but the power is limited because only members of Congress can introduce legislation.[[69]](#cite_note-75)

Dallas Mavericks :: Rivalries :: San Antonio Spurs :: part 01 :: chunk_0034
Main article: [Mavericks–Spurs rivalry](/wiki/Mavericks%E2%80%93Spurs_rivalry "Mavericks–Spurs rivalry")

The Mavericks-Spurs rivalry is relatively new but very fierce. It features two teams with Dallas roots—the Spurs began their life in the [ABA](/wiki/American_Basketball_Association "American Basketball Association") as the Dallas Chaparrals and did not move to San Antonio until 1973. On October 11, 1980, the Mavericks made their NBA debut by defeating the Spurs 103–92. The teams have met numerous times in the playoffs, with the Spurs defeating the Mavericks in 2001, 2003, 2010, and 2014, while the Mavericks defeated the Spurs in 2006 and 2009. The Spurs have won five championships and six conference titles, while the Mavericks have won one championship and three conference titles. The Spurs have won 15 division titles, while the Mavericks have won 5. Both the Spurs and the Mavericks have 3 60-win seasons. This is known as the "I-35 rivalry" because both cities lie on [Interstate 35](/wiki/Interstate_35 "Interstate 35").

The two teams met in the playoffs during the 2000–2001 season with the Spurs winning in five games. Little was made during this series, as the Spurs won their first NBA championship only two years before. The Mavericks, run by a trio of [Steve Nash](/wiki/Steve_Nash "Steve Nash"), [Michael Finley](/wiki/Michael_Finley "Michael Finley"), and [Dirk Nowitzki](/wiki/Dirk_Nowitzki "Dirk Nowitzki"), had just defeated the [Utah Jazz](/wiki/Utah_Jazz "Utah Jazz") despite not having home-court advantage and were only starting to meld into a title contender.

The two teams met again in 2003 in the Western Conference finals. Both the Spurs and the Mavericks had 60-win seasons and reached the Western Conference finals after defeating the [Los Angeles Lakers](/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers") and the [Sacramento Kings](/wiki/Sacramento_Kings "Sacramento Kings"), respecti

In 2013, before the release of *The Amazing Spider-Man 2*, Sony announced a third *Amazing Spider-Man* film with a release date of June 10, 2016, and a fourth film with a release date of May 4, 2018.[[129]](#cite_note-The_Hollywood_Reporter-141)[[130]](#cite_note-142) The third film was to be written by [Alex Kurtzman](/wiki/Alex_Kurtzman "Alex Kurtzman"), [Roberto Orci](/wiki/Roberto_Orci "Roberto Orci"), and [Jeff Pinkner](/wiki/Jeff_Pinkner "Jeff Pinkner"). There were also plans for a two-part [Sinister Six](/wiki/Sinister_Six "Sinister Six") spin-off film written and directed by [Drew Goddard](/wiki/Drew_Goddard "Drew Goddard"), and a [Venom](/wiki/Venom_(character) "Venom (character)") film written by Kurtzman, Orci, and [Ed Solomon](/wiki/Ed_Solomon "Ed Solomon"), and directed by Kurtzman.[[m]](#cite_note-146) Garfield had discussions with Goddard about reprising his role as Spider-Man in *Sinister Six*, which had a planned release date of November 11, 2016.[[n]](#cite_note-150) By August 2014, Sony had hired [Lisa Joy](/wiki/Lisa_Joy "Lisa Joy") to write the script for a 2017 film featuring [Felicia Hardy / Black Cat](/wiki/Black_Cat_(Marvel_Comics) "Black Cat (Marvel Comics)").[[136]](#cite_note-LisaJoyNolan-149) The studio had also announced plans for a [spin-off](/wiki/Spinoff_(media) "Spinoff (media)") based on *[Spider-Man 2099](/wiki/Spider-Man_2099 "Spider-Man 2099")* to be released in late 2017.[[137]](#cite_note-151)

Vatican City :: Name :: chunk_0002
The name *[Vatican City](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Vatican_City "wikt:Vatican City")* was first used in the [Lateran Treaty](/wiki/Lateran_Treaty "Lateran Treaty"), signed on 11 February 1929, which established the modern city-state named after [Vatican Hill](/wiki/Vatican_Hill "Vatican Hill"), the geographic location of the state within the city of [Rome](/wiki/Rome "Rome"). *Vatican* itself is derived from the name of an [Etruscan](/wiki/Etruscan_civilization "Etruscan civilization") settlement, *Vatica* or *Vaticum*, located in the general area the Romans called *[Ager Vaticanus](/wiki/Ager_Vaticanus "Ager Vaticanus")* ('Vatican territory').[[22]](#cite_note-34)

The [Italian-language](/wiki/Italian_language "Italian language") name of the city is *Città del Vaticano* or, more formally, *Stato della Città del Vaticano*, meaning 'State of Vatican City'. Its [Latin](/wiki/Latin "Latin") name is *Status Civitatis Vaticanae*;[[23]](#cite_note-35)[[24]](#cite_note-36) this is used in official documents by the [Holy See](/wiki/Holy_See "Holy See"), the Church and the [pope](/wiki/Pope "Pope").

Further information: [History of the Papacy](/wiki/History_of_the_Papacy "History of the Papacy") and [Holy See § History](/wiki/Holy_See#History "Holy See")

In 1885, [Clinton Thomas Dent](/wiki/Clinton_Thomas_Dent "Clinton Thomas Dent"), president of the [Alpine Club](/wiki/Alpine_Club_(UK) "Alpine Club (UK)"), suggested climbing Everest was possible in his book *Above the Snow Line*.[[103]](#cite_note-111) The northern approach to the mountain was discovered by [George Mallory](/wiki/George_Mallory "George Mallory") and [Guy Bullock](/wiki/Guy_Bullock "Guy Bullock") on the initial [1921 British Reconnaissance Expedition](/wiki/1921_British_Mount_Everest_reconnaissance_expedition "1921 British Mount Everest reconnaissance expedition"). It was not equipped for a serious attempt to climb the mountain. With Mallory leading, and thus becoming the first European to set foot on Everest's flanks, they climbed the North Col to an altitude of 7,005 metres (22,982 ft). From there, Mallory espied a route to the top, but the party was unprepared to climb further and descended. The British returned for a [1922 expedition](/wiki/1922_British_Mount_Everest_expedition "1922 British Mount Everest expedition"). On the first summit attempt Mallory, [Col. Felix Norton](/wiki/Edward_Felix_Norton "Edward Felix Norton"), and [Howard Somervell](/wiki/Howard_Somervell "Howard Somervell") without supplemental oxygen reached 8,225 m (26,985 ft), the first time a human reported to climb higher than 8,000 m (26,247 ft). [George Finch](/wiki/George_Finch_(chemist) "George Finch (chemist)") together with [Geoffrey Bruce](/wiki/Geoffrey_Bruce "Geoffrey Bruce") climbed using oxygen for the first time. They ascended at a remarkable speed—290 metres (951 ft) per hour—and reached an altitude of 8,321 m (27,300 ft).

The [next expedition was in 1924](/wiki/1924_British_Mount_Everest_Expedition "1924 British Mount Everest Expedition"). The initial attempt by Mallory and Geoffrey Bruce was aborted when weather conditions prevented the establishment of Camp VI. The next attempt was by Norton and Som

Jim Kenney :: Mayor of Philadelphia :: First term (2016–2020) :: Opposition to Donald Trump :: chunk_0006
Before and after [Donald Trump](/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump")'s election as President in 2016, Kenney has taken a vocal stand against Trump and his policies. Kenney has maintained that Philadelphia will continue to act as a [sanctuary city](/wiki/Sanctuary_city "Sanctuary city") despite threats that cities would stop receiving federal funding.[[34]](#cite_note-34) Trump said, "Here in Philadelphia, murder has been steady—I mean—just terribly increasing."[[35]](#cite_note-35)

Kenney, along with Democratic colleagues Representative [Dwight Evans](/wiki/Dwight_Evans_(politician) "Dwight Evans (politician)"), Senator [Bob Casey Jr.](/wiki/Bob_Casey_Jr. "Bob Casey Jr."), Councilwoman [Helen Gym](/wiki/Helen_Gym "Helen Gym"), and Governor [Tom Wolf](/wiki/Tom_Wolf "Tom Wolf"), joined protesters at [Philadelphia International Airport](/wiki/Philadelphia_International_Airport "Philadelphia International Airport") after Trump signed [Executive Order 13769](/wiki/Executive_Order_13769 "Executive Order 13769") to ban travel from seven majority-Muslim countries.[[36]](#cite_note-36)

On October 23, 2019, Kenney endorsed [Elizabeth Warren](/wiki/Elizabeth_Warren "Elizabeth Warren") for president in 2020.[[37]](#cite_note-37)

On November 6, while the US awaited the final few results of the 2020 election, Kenney gave remarks aimed at Donald Trump: "What the president needs to do is, frankly, put his big boy pants on, acknowledge that he lost, and congratulate the winner." The statement was made in the interest of the nation moving forwards, and Kenney cited several former presidents and presidential candidates, including [George H. W. Bush](/wiki/George_H._W._Bush "George H. W. Bush"), [Jimmy Carter](/wiki/Jimmy_Carter "Jimmy Carter"), and [Al Gore](/wiki/Al_Gore "Al Gore").[[38]](#cite_note-38)

Mars is approximately half the diameter of Earth or twice that of the Moon, with a surface area only slightly less than the total area of Earth's dry land.[[2]](#cite_note-NasaFactSheet-3) Mars is less dense than Earth, having about 15% of Earth's volume and 11% of Earth's [mass](/wiki/Mass "Mass"), resulting in about 38% of [Earth's surface gravity](/wiki/Gravity_of_Earth "Gravity of Earth"). Mars is the only presently known example of a [desert planet](/wiki/Desert_planet "Desert planet"), a rocky planet with a surface akin to that of Earth's [deserts](/wiki/Desert "Desert"). The red-orange appearance of the Martian surface is caused by [iron(III) oxide](/wiki/Iron(III)_oxide "Iron(III) oxide") ([nanophase](/wiki/Nanophase "Nanophase") Fe2O3) and the [iron(III) oxide-hydroxide](/wiki/Iron(III)_oxide-hydroxide "Iron(III) oxide-hydroxide") mineral [goethite](/wiki/Goethite "Goethite").[[43]](#cite_note-rust-45) It can look like [butterscotch](/wiki/Butterscotch "Butterscotch");[[44]](#cite_note-ismars-46) other common surface colors include golden, brown, tan, and greenish, depending on the [minerals](/wiki/Mineral "Mineral") present.[[44]](#cite_note-ismars-46)

Suits (American TV series) :: Series overview :: Season 5 (2015–16) :: chunk_0007
Main article: [Suits season 5](/wiki/Suits_season_5 "Suits season 5")

Harvey struggles with losing Donna and begins to open up to his therapist Paula Agard about his broken relationship with his mother. Louis's insecurity and desire to undermine Harvey create an opening for Jack Soloff, an ambitious partner whom Hardman is manipulating. Rachel's wedding plans and her relationship with her parents are overshadowed by Mike's secret. Mike and Harvey both resign to protect their future and the firm's respectively, but Mike is abruptly arrested for [fraud](/wiki/Fraud "Fraud"). More and more people involved realize the allegations are true, and facing tenacious federal prosecutor Anita Gibbs, Assistant US Attorney for the US Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York, Mike accepts a [plea bargain](/wiki/Plea_bargain "Plea bargain"), pleads guilty, and turns himself in so that no one else will go to jail. Mike and Rachel decide to get married before he is imprisoned. At the wedding, Mike realizes that it isn't right and tells Rachel that he will not marry her now, but if she still wants him in two years, he will marry her after getting out of prison. Harvey escorts him to prison, saying their last few goodbyes. Jessica, Louis, and Donna return to the firm, but find every employee has left for another firm.

The career achievement of winning all four major championships in one discipline is termed a "Career Grand Slam", or "Career Slam".[[143]](#cite_note-169) In singles, nine men ([Fred Perry](/wiki/Fred_Perry "Fred Perry"), [Don Budge](/wiki/Don_Budge "Don Budge"), [Roy Emerson](/wiki/Roy_Emerson "Roy Emerson"), [Rod Laver](/wiki/Rod_Laver "Rod Laver"), [Andre Agassi](/wiki/Andre_Agassi "Andre Agassi"), [Roger Federer](/wiki/Roger_Federer "Roger Federer"), [Rafael Nadal](/wiki/Rafael_Nadal "Rafael Nadal"), [Novak Djokovic](/wiki/Novak_Djokovic "Novak Djokovic") and [Carlos Alcaraz](/wiki/Carlos_Alcaraz "Carlos Alcaraz")) and ten women ([Maureen Connolly](/wiki/Maureen_Connolly "Maureen Connolly"), [Doris Hart](/wiki/Doris_Hart "Doris Hart"), [Shirley Fry Irvin](/wiki/Shirley_Fry_Irvin "Shirley Fry Irvin"), [Margaret Court](/wiki/Margaret_Court "Margaret Court"), [Billie Jean King](/wiki/Billie_Jean_King "Billie Jean King"), [Chris Evert](/wiki/Chris_Evert "Chris Evert"), [Martina Navratilova](/wiki/Martina_Navratilova "Martina Navratilova"), [Steffi Graf](/wiki/Steffi_Graf "Steffi Graf"), [Serena Williams](/wiki/Serena_Williams "Serena Williams"), and [Maria Sharapova](/wiki/Maria_Sharapova "Maria Sharapova")) have completed a Career Grand Slam.[[2]](#cite_note-CGS-2) Four men (Emerson, Laver, Djokovic, and Nadal) and five women (Court, Evert, Navratilova, Graf, Williams) have achieved the feat more than once over the course of their careers.[[144]](#cite_note-170)[[145]](#cite_note-171)[[146]](#cite_note-:5-172)
